context:
Make the audit a check, not a one-off doc. The two scripts already exist
and are proven; promoting them is mostly file moves + an allowlist
surface + a Makefile target + a CI job hook.

The allowlists are the load-bearing design choice. They MUST mirror the
inventory doc's exemptions exactly, and a comment in each allowlist
entry should reference the audit finding or transitive-via annotation
that justifies it.
description:
The `audit-imported-dependencies-for-elimination` audit was driven by
two methodology scripts currently parked under `_project/scratch/`
(gitignored):
  - `parse_deps.py` - tomllib-based dep enumeration from pyproject.toml
  - `scan_imports.py` - AST walker over benchbox/, scripts/, tests/,
    docs/conf.py, docs/_static/

Without a check, the audit's "70 KEEP, 6 FLAG-*" snapshot decays. New
unused deps drift in; new top-level imports go undeclared. This TODO
promotes those scripts into a real CI guard so the audit stays current
for free.

Source: parent TODO `tighten-dependencies-phase-plan` (Phase 4) and
`docs/development/dependency-inventory.md` Methodology section.

Run the new check locally against current main; confirm it passes (i.e. agrees with the audit's KEEP/FLAG verdict). If it disagrees, reconcile the allowlists.
Update `docs/development/dependency-inventory.md` Methodology section to point at the tracked scripts and to document `make audit-deps` as the canonical re-run mechanism.
